messages:
support-miguel: Hey team — Collectly support ticket #C-9642. They're seeing a spike in 5xx / timeouts hitting hosted API since ~2026-03-17 06:10 UTC. Customer says p95 requests time out and many end up with 504 gateway errors. They provided traces and a short repro (below). Can someone triage asap? :rotating_light:

customer-ops-jenny: Customer repro steps (from their ops): 1) open 200 simultaneous short-chat requests (avg 120 tokens) over a 30s window to model rwd-small. 2) observe error spike after ~40s. Curl snippet they used: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hi"}'; done` — attached trace ids: trace:ab12, trace:ab13. They say this only started this morning after an internal traffic change.

sre-jordan: Thanks. Are these 504s originating from our gateway (NLB/nginx) or from the inference pods? Any 200s with very long downstream times?

observability-bot: metric snapshot @06:12 UTC: `ingress.request_queue_depth` (hosted-prod): 0.92 (92% of configured max), `continuous_batch.pending_requests`: 1248, `dequeue_latency_p99`: 2.8s, `request_enqueue_time_p95`: 1.1s. Error rate 5xx went from 0.4% -> 7.6% between 06:09-06:14. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/ingress/queue-depth?from=2026-03-17T06:00Z

eng-runtime-kate: Logged the trace ids. Grepping runtime logs shows many `ENQUEUE` events followed by long `BATCH_WAIT` and then `DEQUEUE_FAIL: deadline_exceeded` for tenant collectly-tenant-id. Snippet: ```
[06:11:18] ENQUEUE req=tx=ab12 tenant=collectly size=120
[06:11:20] BATCH_WAIT batch=42 wait_ms=2100
[06:11:42] DEQUEUE_FAIL tx=ab12 reason=deadline_exceeded
```
This looks like continuous-batching backlog + queue depth configured too low -> long tail wait then gateway 504s.

infra-bot: Alert: `queue_depth_threshold_exceeded` tenant=collectly-tenant-id pool=hosted-prod severity=high. Auto-escalation to oncall.

eng-platform-lee: Quick note — we recently tightened `ingress.max_queue_depth` to reduce memory pressure (rolled 03-17 02:00 UTC). That change would make the system hit backpressure earlier on bursty short requests. Possible regression.

sre-jordan: Hypothesis: burst of many short, latency-sensitive requests fills the continuous-batcher queue; batching waits to reach batch size or window so short requests pile and hit queue depth limit. System tries to serve but dequeue latency spikes and gateway times out producers -> 504s.

support-miguel: Customer is asking for an ETA and workaround. They prefer not to move to Dedicated right away.

eng-runtime-kate: Short-term mitigations to propose to support: 1) enable tenant-level `ingress.reject_on_depth=true` to fail fast instead of stall (reduces 504 tail). 2) decrease `batch_window_ms` for this tenant to favor latency over throughput. 3) as emergency, route their tenant to a less-busy pool or spin up extra burst capacity. We can patch the runtime config and canary it to the tenant.

sre-jordan: Agreed. Also lower `max_queue_depth` per-tenant was a regression for bursty low-token workloads; we should revert for hosted-prod or add adaptive per-workload profiles. For now let's apply option 1 + 2 for Collectly and monitor.

customer-ops-jenny: Please note: customer still hitting 504s on every 15-20th request in the burst. If you need to test, use the same burst script — they can run in our staging tenant.

eng-platform-lee: I'll roll a canary: set `collectly-tenant-id.ingress.reject_on_depth=true` and `collectly-tenant-id.batch_window_ms=8` (was 20). Patching now. Will monitor for 10m then expand.

observability-bot: Canary applied at 06:29 UTC. New metric snapshot: `ingress.request_queue_depth` for collectly down to 0.45, `dequeue_latency_p99` -> 0.9s. Error rate dropped to 1.1% in the next 5m.

support-miguel: Customer confirms fewer 504s after the change — reporting best-effort evenness. They asked if this will be permanent.

eng-runtime-kate: Follow-ups: 1) revert the global `max_queue_depth` rollback we did earlier or make it workload-aware. 2) add tenant-level defaults for small-token workloads to favor latency. 3) add a synthetic load test for short bursty chat workloads to catch regressions. I'll open PRs for 1 & 2 and a test job for 3.

sre-jordan: I'll coordinate a retro and include runbook updates: how to toggle `reject_on_depth` and safe batch_window ranges per model.

eng-platform-lee: Action items assigned: platform will keep canary for 30m then schedule platform-wide mitigation or targeted revert. eng-runtime will prepare config validation/safer defaults. support to follow up with Collectly and close ticket after 24h stable.

support-miguel: Thanks all. Pinging @customer-ops-jenny to confirm close after 24h of stable metrics. :thumbsup:
